title: Musical Composition & Cultural Milestones: Megzenésít, megalkot, szimbólumává válik

sections.title: Connecting European and Hungarian Music History
sections.content: You know the translative *-vá/-vé* with *válik* from A2 Unit 35; here it appears in *szimbólumává válik* ('becomes the symbol of'). New verbs for talking about music: *megzenésít* ('sets a poem to music'), *megteremt* ('creates, founds') and *megalkot* ('creates'). You also met Liszt, Bartók and Kodály in B1 Unit 68.

sections.title: The composers of this lesson (explained)
rows: German Baroque master: his organ fugues, Brandenburg Concertos, and St Matthew Passion (Máté-passió) are major works of Baroque polyphony and Christian sacred music.
Prodigy of Viennese Classicism (bécsi klasszicizmus): his operas The Magic Flute (A varázsfuvola) and Don Giovanni and his symphonies combine clear melody with dramatic characterisation.
Bridge from Classicism to Romanticism: composing even after losing his hearing, he set Schiller's Ode to Joy (Örömóda) in his Ninth Symphony — today the official anthem of the European Union.
Often called the founder of Hungarian national opera (Hunyadi László, Bánk bán — with the aria 'Hazám, hazám'); he composed the music of Kölcsey's Himnusz in 1844.
Liszt Ferenc, Bartók Béla és Kodály Zoltán

Liszt brought the Hungarian Rhapsodies to European concert halls and became the first president of the Zeneakadémia (founded 1875); Bartók and Kodály collected peasant folk songs to renew 20th-century music and music education.

items.spanish: Beethoven IX. szimfóniájának Örömóda-dallama az Európai Unió himnuszává vált.
items.english: The Ode to Joy melody of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony became the anthem of the European Union.

items.spanish: Erkel Ferenc 1844-ben zenésítette meg Kölcsey Ferenc Himnusz című költeményét.
items.english: Ferenc Erkel set Ferenc Kölcsey's poem Himnusz to music in 1844.

items.spanish: Mozart és Beethoven a bécsi klasszicizmus legismertebb zeneszerzői voltak.
items.english: Mozart and Beethoven were the best-known composers of Viennese Classicism.
